newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition leader threatens government.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition leader threatens government.

text.p: Bangladesh opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Tuesday threatened to mount a mass campaign to topple the government unless it freed all detained opponents and behaved more democratically.

"We will be forced to launch a massive and drastic movement to pull down the corrupt and autocratic government," she told tens of thousands of supporters of her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) at a rally.
"We are giving the government of (Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina) an ultimatum to accept our demands or face a bitter challenge," Khaleda told cheering followers.
"Meanwhile, I urge the people to get ready for a movement to be launched after the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan (starting on Monday)."
It was the first major rally organised by the BNP since it lost a general election last June to Hasina's Awami League, and coincided with a visit to Dhaka by Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The BNP's demands include the release of all political detainees and the withdrawal of charges against BNP leaders and workers.
Khaleda said Hasina's government in the past six months had virtually destroyed the country's economy and was trying to impose one-party rule.
"The country has been turned into a free market for foreign goods, especially from India," Khaleda said.
"But the people of Bangladesh will not tolerate any conspiracy to undermine their country's freedom and independence," she added.
India helped Bangladesh win a 1971 war of independence against Pakistan.
Khaleda said "apart from talking, no local or foreign investment has actually come or been used in the country since the change of government".
"This is because no one has confidence in Hasina's fragile government pursuing a wrong economic policy."
Badruddoza Chowdhury, deputy leader of the BNP, said India was trying to turn Bangladesh into a subservient nation.
He criticised Deve Gowda for not meeting Khaleda Zia during his Bangladesh visit.
"You are siding with a weak, corrupt and subservient party (Awami League). Otherwise you would not have escaped seeing our leader," he said.
